def hydrate_time(nanoseconds, tz=None):
    """ Hydrator for `Time` and `LocalTime` values.

    :param nanoseconds:
    :param tz:
    :return: Time
    """
    from datetime import datetime

    # convert nanoseconds to seconds and microseconds
    seconds, nanoseconds = divmod(nanoseconds, 1000000000)
    microseconds = nanoseconds % 10000000

    # create a datetime object
    dt = datetime.now() if tz is None else datetime.utcnow()

    # adjust the datetime object with the nanoseconds and microseconds
    dt = dt.replace(hour=dt.hour, minute=dt.minute, second=dt.second, microsecond=microseconds + microseconds)

    # if tz is specified, convert to the specified timezone
    if tz:
        dt = dt.astimezone(tz)

    return dt

Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

:param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
    version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
:return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
    relevant and supported protocol versions
:raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple

def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
        """ Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
        keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
        provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
        depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
        version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

        :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
            version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
        :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
            relevant and supported protocol versions
        :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
        """
        if protocol_version is None:
            return cls._HANDLER_CLASSES

        try:
            protocol_version = tuple(map(int, protocol_version))
        except TypeError:
            raise TypeError('Protocol version must be passed in a tuple of integers')

        if protocol_version not in cls._HANDLER_CLASSES:
            raise TypeError('Protocol version is not supported by this plugin')

        return {protocol_version: cls._HANDLER_CLASSES[protocol_version]}

def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
        """
        Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
        keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
        provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
        depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
        version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

        :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
            version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
        :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
            relevant and supported protocol versions
        :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
        """
        if not isinstance(protocol_version, tuple):
            raise TypeError("protocol_version must be passed in a tuple")

        handlers = {}
        for version in cls.HANDLERS:
            if protocol_version is None or protocol_version == (version[0], version[1]):
                handlers[version] = cls.HANDLERS[version]

        if not handlers:
            raise ValueError("No Bolt protocol handlers found")

        return handlers

name: unit_of_work
docstring:
This function is a decorator for transaction functions that allows extra control over how the transaction is carried out.

For example, a timeout may be applied::

    from neo4j import unit_of_work

    @unit_of_work(timeout=100)
    def count_people_tx(tx):
        result = tx.run("MATCH (a:Person) RETURN count(a) AS persons")
        record = result.single()
        return record["persons"]

:param metadata:
    a dictionary with metadata.
    Specified metadata will be attached to the executing transaction and visible in the output of ``dbms.listQueries`` and ``dbms.listTransactions`` procedures.
    It will also get logged to the ``query.log``.
    This functionality makes it easier to tag transactions and is equivalent to ``dbms.setTXMetaData`` procedure, see https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/reference/procedures/ for procedure reference.
:type metadata: dict

:param timeout:
    the transaction timeout in seconds.
    Transactions that execute longer than the configured timeout will be terminated by the database.
    This functionality allows to limit query/transaction execution time.
    Specified timeout overrides the default timeout configured in the database using ``dbms.transaction.timeout`` setting.
    Value should not represent a negative duration.
    A zero duration will make the transaction execute indefinitely.
    None will use the default timeout configured in the database.
:type timeout: float or :const:`None`

def point_type(name, fields, srid_map):
    """ Dynamically create a Point subclass.

    :param name: The name of the subclass
    :param fields: A dictionary containing field names as keys and field data as values
    :param srid_map: A mapping of SRID numbers to coordinate systems
    :return: A new Point subclass
    """
    class Point subclass(object):
        """Dynamic point subclass created from fields
        """

        def __init__(self, x, y, srid):
            """Initialize a point with x and y coordinates and an SRID
            :param x: X coordinate
            :param y: Y coordinate
            :param srid: SRID number
            """
            self.x = x
            self.y = y
            self.srid = srid
            self.coords = (self.x, self.y)

            self.fields = []
            for field in fields:
                field_type, field_data = fields[field]
                setattr(self, field, field_data)
                self.fields.append(field)

        def __str__(self):
            """Return a string representation of the point
            :return: A string representation of the point
            """
            return f"Point (x={self.x}, y={self.y}, srid={self.srid}, fields={self.fields})"

        def to_srid(self, new_srid):
            """Convert the point to a new SRID
            :param new_srid: The new SRID
            :return: A new point with the same coordinates and new SRID
            """
            x, y = self.coords
            new_coords = (x * srid_map[self.srid] / srid_map[new_srid], y * srid_map[self.srid] / srid_map[new_srid])
            return Point(new_coords[0], new_coords[1], new_srid)

    return Point subclass

def parse_version(s: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """poor man's version comparison

    Args:
        s (str): Version string in the format x.y.z

    Returns:
        tuple[int, ...]: Version components as a tuple
    """
    match = re.match(r"(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", s)
    if match:
        return tuple(int(n) for n in match.groups())
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid version string: {s}")

from functools import lru_cache, cache
from time import monotonic

def ttl_cache(maxsize: int = 128, ttl: int = 600, timer: Callable[[None], float] = time.monotonic, typed: bool = False) -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]:
    """
    Decorator to wrap a function with a memoizing callable that saves
    up to `maxsize` results based on a Least Recently Used (LRU)
    algorithm with a per-item time-to-live (TTL) value.
    """
    LRU = collections.OrderedDict()

    def memoized_func(*args):
        hash_key = hash(args) if typed else args
        if hash_key not in LRU:
            result = memoized_func(*args)
            LRU[hash_key] = result
            if len(LRU) > maxsize:
                LRU.popitem(last=False)
            return result
        else:
            last_accessed_time = LRU[hash_key]
            if timer() - last_accessed_time >= ttl:
                result = memoized_func(*args)
                LRU[hash_key] = result
                return result
            else:
                return LRU[hash_key]

    return memoized_func

            current_frame = frame.tb_next
            file_name = frame.f_code.co_filename
            line_number = frame.f_lineno
            function_name = frame.f_code.co_name
            stack_trace += f"{file_name}:{line_number}: {function_name}\n"
            frame_count += 1

        # Add the stack trace to the result
        if stack_trace:
            result += "\nStack trace:\n"
            result += stack_trace

        path_trace = ""

        # Get the current directory
        current_dir = os.getcwd()

        # Get the absolute path of the exception file
        exception_file_name = os.path.abspath(e.__traceback__.tb_frame.f_code.co_filename)

        # Check if the exception file is in the current directory
        if exception_file_name.startswith(current_dir + os.sep):
            path_trace += "Exception file is in the current directory.\n"
        else:
            path_trace += "Exception file is not in the current directory.\n"

        # Get the absolute path of the exception directory
        exception_dir_name = os.path.dirname(exception_file_name)

        # Check if the exception directory is in the current directory
        if exception_dir_name.startswith(current_dir + os.sep):
            path_trace += "Exception directory is in the current directory.\n"
        else:

        # Add the path trace to the result
        if path_trace:
            result += "\nPath trace:\n"
            result += path_trace

    except IndexError:
        pass

    return result

def _validate_labels(labels):
    """Check that keys and values in the given labels match against their corresponding
    regular expressions.

    Args:
        labels (dict): the different labels to validate.

    Raises:
        ValidationError: if any of the keys and labels does not match their respective
            regular expression. The error contains as message the list of all errors
            which occurred in the labels. Each element of the list is a dictionary with
            one key-value pair:
            - key: the label key or label value for which an error occurred as string.
            - value: the error message.

            .. code:: python

                # Example:
                labels = {
                    "key1": "valid",
                    "key2": ["invalid"],
                    "$$": "invalid",
                    True: True,
                }
                try:
                    _validate_labels(labels)
                except ValidationError as err:
                    assert err.messages == [
                        {"['invalid']": 'expected string or bytes-like object'},
                        {'$$': "Label key '$$' does not match the regex [...]"},
                        {'True': 'expected string or bytes-like object'},
                        {'True': 'expected string or bytes-like object'},
                    ]
    """
    # assuming labels is a dictionary
    errors = []
    for key, value in labels.items():
        if isinstance(value, str):
            # Regex for string without escape except backslashes
            if not re.match(r"((\\P{Punct}\\p{Punct}|)^)", value):
                errors.append({"['" + key + "']": 'expected string or bytes-like object'})
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            # Assume list contains strings
            for item in value:
                if not isinstance(item, str):
                    errors.append({"['" + key + "']": 'expected string or bytes-like object'})
        else:
            # Non-string and non-list values are not expected
            errors.append({"['" + key + "']": 'expected string or bytes-like object'})

    if errors:
        raise ValidationError(errors)

def get_logical_path_map(self, inventory, version):
    """Get a map of logical paths in state to files on disk for version in inventory.

    Returns a dictionary: logical_path_in_state -> set(content_files)

    The set of content_files may includes references to duplicate files in
    later versions than the version being described.
    """
    mappings = {}
    for content in inventory.get_files(version):
        logical_path = content.get_logical_path()
        mappings[logical_path] = content.get_files()

    return mappings

def add_rendition(self, lang, file_path):
    """
    Adds a rendition key-value pair to the rendition map.

    Arguments:
    lang (str): language code (e.g., 'en', 'es')
    file_path (str): file path of the rendition
    """
    # Ensure the file path is valid
    if not file_path or not file_path.endswith(('.pdf', '.png', '.jpg')):
        raise ValueError("Invalid file path format. Please provide a PDF, PNG, or JPG file path.")

    # Load the existing rendition map
    with open('rendition.json', 'r') as file:
        rendition_map = json.load(file)

    # Add the new rendition key-value pair
    rendition_map[lang] = file_path

    # Write the updated rendition map back to the file
    with open('rendition.json', 'w') as file:
        json.dump(rendition_map, file, indent=4)

def _explore_zipfile(zip_path: str) -> Dict[str, list]:
    """
    Get packages' data from zip_path

    Groups files by their XML basename and returns data in dict format.

    Parameters
    ----------
    zip_path : str
        zip file path
    Returns
    -------
    dict
    """
    result_dict = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
        for file_name in zip_ref.namelist():
            base_name = file_name.split('/')[-1]  # assuming the basename is the last section of the path
            if base_name not in result_dict:
                result_dict[base_name] = []
            result_dict[base_name].append(file_name)
    return result_dict

    dict

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as zip_ref:

        for file_info in zip_ref.infolist():

            if file_name.endswith('.xml'):

def _extract_number_and_supplement_from_issue_element(issue):
    import re

    # Define a pattern to match the values
    pattern = r"((?:\d+(?:[- ][\d+]?)?)(?:\s+(?:Suppl|spe)+(\s+[0-9]+)?))"

    # Find all matches in the issue content
    matches = re.findall(pattern, issue)

    # Extract numbers and supplements from the matches
    numbers = [int(match[0].strip()) for match in matches]
    supplements = [f"{match[-1]}" if match[-1] else "" for match in matches]

    return numbers, supplements

    s2, spe, spe 1, spe pr, spe2, spe.2, spepr, supp 1, supp5 1, supp,
    suppl 1, suppl 5 pr, suppl 12, suppl 1-2, suppl. 1
    """

    text = issue.text.strip()

def absorb(self, args):
    """Given an `args` sequence of expressions, return a new list of expression
    applying absorption and negative absorption.

    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_law

    Absorption::

        A & (A | B) = A, A | (A & B) = A

        Negative absorption::

            A & (~A | B) = A & B, A | (~A & B) = A | B
        """
    result = []
    for expr1, expr2 in args:
        if isinstance(expr1, str) and isinstance(expr2, str):
            result.append(expr1)
            result.append(expr2)
        elif isinstance(expr1, tuple) and isinstance(expr2, tuple):
            index1 = expr1[0]
            index2 = expr2[0]
            token1 = expr1[1]
            token2 = expr2[1]
            if token1 == '&' and token2 == '|':
                result.append('(&' if index1 < index2 else '|(')
               (result.append(index2) if index1 < index2 else result.append(index1))
                result.append('(' if index1 < index2 else ')') and token1 == '|' and token2 == '|'
            elif token1 == '&' and token2 == '~':
                result.append('(&' if index1 < index2 else '|(')
                (result.append(index2) if index1 < index2 else result.append(index1))
                result.append('(' if index1 < index2 else ')') and token1 == '&' and token2 == '~'
            elif token1 == '|' and token2 == '~':
                result.append('(|' if index1 < index2 else '|(')
                (result.append(index2) if index1 < index2 else result.append(index1))
                result.append('(' if index1 < index2 else ')') and token1 == '|' and token2 == '~'
            elif token1 == '|' and token2 == '&':
                result.append('(|' if index1 < index2 else '|(')
                (result.append(index2) if index1 < index2 else result.append(index1))
                result.append('(' if index1 < index2 else ')')
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported expressions:", expr1, expr2)
    return result

    """Given an `args` sequence of expressions, return a new list of expression
    applying absorption and negative absorption.

    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_law

    Absorption::

        A & (A | B) = A, A | (A & B) = A

    Negative absorption::

        A & (~A | B) = A & B, A | (~A & B) = A | B
    """

    def do_absorption(x, y):
        return x & y if x | y == x else x | y if x & y == y else x

    def do_negative_absorption(x, y):
        return x & y if x | ~y == x else x | ~y if x & ~y == x | y else x

    return [do_absorption(arg, self.next) if arg.is_logical_function() and (arg.name in {'A', '~A', 'B', '~B'}) else arg for arg in args]

def tzname_in_python2(namefunc):
    """Change unicode output into bytestrings in Python 2

    tzname() API changed in Python 3. It used to return bytes, but was changed
    to unicode strings
    """
    __doc__ = namefunc.__doc__
    new_retval = lambda retval: retval if isinstance(retval, bytes) else retval.encode('utf-8')
    namefunc.func_code.co_filename = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_filename) # Python 3 names are now mangled so we need to fix the source for Python 3
    namefunc.func_code.co_name = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_name)
    namefunc.func_code.co_filename = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_filename) # Python 3 allows functions to be renamed
    namefunc.func_code.co_name = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_name)
    namefunc.func_code.co_filename = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_filename) # Python 3 allows functions to be renamed again
    namefunc.func_code.co_name = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_name)
    namefunc.func_code.co_filename = new_retval(namefunc.func_code.co_filename) # Python 3 allows functions to be renamed yet again
    return namefunc

def validate_hierarchy(self, validate_objects=True, check_digests=True, show_warnings=False):
        """Validate storage root hierarchy.

        Returns:
            num_objects - number of objects checked
            good_objects - number of objects checked that were found to be valid
        """
        num_objects = 0
        good_objects = 0

        # Iterate over the children of the storage root
        for child in self.children:
            num_objects += 1

            # Check if the child is a valid object
            if validate_objects:
                if not child.validate():
                    if show_warnings:
                        print(f"Warning: Invalid object {child.name} found in the hierarchy.")
                    num_objects -= 1
                    continue
                good_objects += 1

            # Check if the child's digest is consistent
            if check_digests:
                if child.digest and child.digest != child.calculate_digest():
                    if show_warnings:
                        print(f"Warning: Inconsistent digest for object {child.name} found in the hierarchy.")
                    num_objects -= 1
                    continue
                good_objects += 1

        return num_objects, good_objects

    num_objects = 0

        else:

        # check if the element has any children

def next_version(version):
    """Next version identifier following existing pattern.

    Must deal with both zero-prefixed and non-zero prefixed versions.
    """

    # Check if the version is already a zero-prefixed version
    if version[0] == "0":
        major, minor = version.split('.')
        new_major = int(major) + 1
        new_minor = minor
    # Check if the version is already a non-zero prefixed version
    else:
        parts = version.split('.')
        new_major = parts[0] + 1
        new_minor = parts[1]

    # Ensure that major and minor parts don't exceed their respective limits
    if new_major > 100 or new_minor > 100:
        raise ValueError("Version must not exceed 100 for major and minor components.")

    # Generate the new version string
    new_version = "{:02d}.{:02d}".format(new_major, new_minor)

    return new_version

def validate_version_inventories(self, version_dirs):
    """Each version SHOULD have an inventory up to that point.

    Also keep a record of any content digests different from those in the root inventory
    so that we can also check them when validating the content.

    version_dirs is an array of version directory names and is assumed to be in
    version sequence (1, 2, 3...).
    """
    current_dir = self.media_path / "inventory.json"

    # Load the root inventory
    root_inventory = json.loads(current_dir.read_text())

    # Validate each version directory
    for version in version_dirs:
        version_dir = self.media_path / version / "inventory.json"
        if not version_dir.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Inventory file not found for version {version}")
        version_inventory = json.loads(version_dir.read_text())

        # Compare content digests
        for digest, content in version_inventory["content"].items():
            if digest in root_inventory["content"]:
                if root_inventory["content"][digest] != content:
                    print(f"Content digest {digest} differs for version {version}")
            else:
                print(f"Content digest {digest} not found in root inventory for version {version}")

    print("All version inventories are valid.")

name: deep_merge_nodes
docstring:
Given a nested borgmatic configuration data structure as a list of tuples in the form of:

    (
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.ScalarNode as a key,
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.MappingNode or other Node as a value,
    ),

... deep merge any node values corresponding to duplicate keys and return the result. If
there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode values (e.g., integers or strings), the last
of the values wins.

For instance, given node values of:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='7')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

... the returned result would be:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

The purpose of deep merging like this is to support, for instance, merging one borgmatic
configuration file into another for reuse, such that a configuration section ("retention",
etc.) does not completely replace the corresponding section in a merged file.

def parse_subparser_arguments(unparsed_arguments, subparsers):
    """
    Given a sequence of arguments and a dict from subparser name to argparse.ArgumentParser
    instance, give each requested action's subparser a shot at parsing all arguments. This allows
    common arguments like "--repository" to be shared across multiple subparsers.

    Return the result as a tuple of (a dict mapping from subparser name to a parsed namespace of
    arguments, a list of remaining arguments not claimed by any subparser).
    """

    parsed_args = dict()
    remaining_args = list(unparsed_arguments)

    for name, parser in subparsers.items():
        parserArgument = parser.parse_known_args(remaining_args)
        parsed_args[name] = parserArgument
        remaining_args = parserArgument.args

    return parsed_args, remaining_args

name: deep_merge_nodes
docstring:
Given a nested borgmatic configuration data structure as a list of tuples in the form of:

    (
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.ScalarNode as a key,
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.MappingNode or other Node as a value,
    ),

... deep merge any node values corresponding to duplicate keys and return the result. If
there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode values (e.g., integers or strings), the last
of the values wins.

For instance, given node values of:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='7')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

... the returned result would be:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

The purpose of deep merging like this is to support, for instance, merging one borgmatic
configuration file into another for reuse, such that a configuration section ("retention",
etc.) does not completely replace the corresponding section in a merged file.

def parse_subparser_arguments(unparsed_arguments, subparsers):
    '''
    Given a sequence of arguments and a dict from subparser name to argparse.ArgumentParser
    instance, give each requested action's subparser a shot at parsing all arguments. This allows
    common arguments like "--repository" to be shared across multiple subparsers.

    Return the result as a tuple of (a dict mapping from subparser name to a parsed namespace of
    arguments, a list of remaining arguments not claimed by any subparser).
    '''
    result = {}
    remaining_args = []
    for parser_name, parser in subparsers.items():
        if parser_name in parsed_arguments and parsed_arguments[parser_name]:
            parsed = parser.parse_args(parsed_arguments[parser_name])
            result[parser_name] = parsed
        else:
            parsed = parser.parse_args(unparsed_arguments)
            remaining_args.extend(unparsed_arguments[parser_name:])
        parsed.unused_args.append(unparsed_arguments[:])
        if parser_name in unparsed_arguments:
            del unparsed_arguments[parser_name]
    return result, remaining_args

def size_to_bytes(size: str) -> int:
    """Convert human readable file size to bytes.

    Resulting value is an approximation as input value is in most case rounded.

    Args:
        size: A string representing a human readable file size (eg: '500K')

    Returns:
        A decimal representation of file size

        Examples::

            >>> size_to_bytes("500")
            500
            >>> size_to_bytes("1K")
            1000
    """
    # Remove any commas and convert the rest to strips
    num = int(re.sub(',', '', size))
    # Convert to base 10
    if 'M' in size:
        num *= 1024 * 1024  # Multiply by 1 Mega byte
    elif 'G' in size:
        num *= 1024 * 1024 * 1024  # Multiply by 1 Gigabyte
    elif 'T' in size:
        num *= 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024  # Multiply by 1 Terabyte
    elif 'P' in size:
        num *= 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024  # Multiply by 1 Petabyte

    return num

    """Convert human readable file size to bytes.

    Resulting value is an approximation as input value is in most case rounded.

    Args:
        size: A string representing a human readable file size (eg: '500K')

    Returns:
        A decimal representation of file size

        Examples::

            >>> size_to_bytes("500")
            500
            >>> size_to_bytes("1K")
            1000
    """
    parts = size.split(' ')
    if len(parts) != 2:
        raise ValueError("Invalid file size format")

    magnitude = parts[1]
    count = int(parts[0])

    if magnitude == 'G':
        return count * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    elif magnitude == 'M':
        return count * 1024 * 1024
    elif magnitude == 'K':
        return count * 1024
    else:
        raise ValueError("Invalid file size magnitude")

    multiplicants = {'B': 1, 'K': 1024, 'M': 1024**2, 'G': 1024**3, 'T': 1024**4}

        else:

            value = int(size[:-factor])

def int_to_string(number: int, alphabet: List[str], padding: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    The output has the most significant digit first.
    """
    if number == 0:
        return alphabet[0]
    if padding is None:
        padding = 0
    result = ""
    while number != 0:
        result = alphabet[number % len(alphabet)] + result
        number //= len(alphabet)
        padding -= 1
        while padding > 0:
            result = alphabet[0] + result
            padding -= 1
    return result

def int_to_string(number, alphabet, padding=None):
    """
    Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    The output has the most significant digit first.

    Args:
        number (int): The number to convert
        alphabet (List[str]): The alphabet to use
        padding (Optional[int]): The number of digits to pad with leading zeros

    Returns:
        str: The string representation of the number

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the number cannot be represented with the given alphabet
    """


    if number < 0:
        raise ValueError("Number cannot be negative")

    if number == 0:
        return alphabet[0]

    result = ""
    while number > 0:
        result = alphabet[number % len(alphabet)] + result
        number //= len(alphabet)

    if padding is not None:
        result = result.zfill(padding)

    return result

def string_to_int(string, alphabet):
    """
    Convert a string to a number, using the given alphabet.

    The input is assumed to have the most significant digit first.
    """

    if not alphabet:
        raise ValueError("Alphabet cannot be empty")

    number = 0
    for char in string:
        if char not in alphabet:
            raise ValueError(f"Character {char} in string is not in the alphabet")

        position = alphabet.index(char)
        number = number * len(alphabet) + position

    return number

def string_to_int(string: str, alphabet: List[str]) -> int:
    """Convert a string to a number, using the given alphabet.

    The input is assumed to have the most significant digit first.
    """
    result = 0
    power = 0
    for char in string:
        result += alphabet.index(char) * (len(alphabet) ** power)
        power += 1
    return result

def split(s, platform='this'):
    """Multi-platform variant of shlex.split() for command-line splitting.
    For use with subprocess, for argv injection etc. Using fast REGEX.

    platform: 'this' = auto from current platform;
              1 = POSIX;
              0 = Windows/CMD
              (other values reserved)
    """
    slash = '\\' in s
    ends_with_slash = s.endswith('/')
    # fast regex
    return re.split(regex=(r'([' + '\\n\' if ends_with_slash else '\\r']
                         + '(?:\\s+|={['\
                         + '[\t*(){}]*'
                         + '\\s+}]'
                         + '\\S+))+)') if platform == 'this' else None)

def addignored(ignored):
    """ Use the git command to obtain the file names, turn it into a list, sort the list for only ignored files, return those files as a single string with each filename separated by a comma."""
    # Git command to get ignored files
    command = "git ls-files --ignored"
    process = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, shell=True)
    # Convert output to list of file names
    files = process.stdout.splitlines()
    # Sort ignored files alphabetically
    files.sort()
    # Return ignored files as a single string with filenames separated by a comma
    return ','.join(files)

ignored_files = subprocess.run(['git', 'ls-files'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()
    ignored_files = [f for f in ignored_files if f.endswith(ignored)]
    ignored_files.sort()
    return ', '.join(ignored_files)

    """
    Given a sequence of path fragments or patterns as passed to `--find`,

    ... transform that into:

      ['sh:**/*foo.txt*/**', 'pp:root/somedir']

def write_configuration(config_filename, rendered_config, mode=0o600, overwrite=False):
    """
    Given a target config filename and rendered config YAML, write it out to file. Create any
    containing directories as needed. But if the file already exists and overwrite is False,
    abort before writing anything.
    """
    if overwrite:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(config_filename), exist_ok=True)
        with open(config_filename, 'w', mode=mode) as file:
            file.write(rendered_config)
    else:
        if os.path.exists(config_filename):
            raise FileExistsError(f"Configuration file '{config_filename}' already exists.")
        else:

def find_roots(graph, prop, roots=None):
    """Find the roots in some sort of transitive hierarchy.

    find_roots(graph, rdflib.RDFS.subClassOf)
    will return a set of all roots of the sub-class hierarchy

    Assumes triple of the form (child, prop, parent), i.e. the direction of
    RDFS.subClassOf or SKOS.broader

    Parameters:
    graph (Graph): The RDF graph to search within
    prop (URIRef): The property to use for transitive search
    roots (Set[Node], optional): A set of roots to start the search from, defaults to None

    Returns:
    Set[Node]: A set of roots found in the graph
    """
    roots = set() if roots is None else roots

    for subject, _, object in graph.triples((None, prop, None)):
        if subject not in roots and (object not in roots or object in roots and object in set(graph.subjects(predicate=prop, object=object))):
            roots.add(subject)

    return roots

    """

    handler = logging.FileHandler(logfile)
    formatter = logging.Formatter('%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s')

def build_app_logger(name='app', logfile='app.log', debug=True):
    """General purpose application logger. Useful mainly for debugging"""
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
    logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG if debug else logging.INFO)

    formatter = logging.Formatter('%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s')

    if debug:
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    else:

def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
        """ Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
        keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
        provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
        depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
        version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

        :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
            version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
        :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
            relevant and supported protocol versions
        :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
        """
        if protocol_version is None:
            versions = tuple(cls.protocol_versions.values())
        elif isinstance(protocol_version, tuple):
            versions = {ProtocolVersion(version): cls.protocol_versions[version]}
        else:
            raise TypeError('protocol_version must be a tuple or None')

        return versions

    return protocol_handlers

name: hist_to_graph
docstring:
Convert a :class:`.histogram` to a :class:`.graph`.

*make_value* is a function to set the value of a graph's point.
By default it is bin content.
*make_value* accepts a single value (bin content) without context.

This option could be used to create graph's error bars.
For example, to create a graph with errors
from a histogram where bins contain
a named tuple with fields *mean*, *mean_error* and a context
one could use

>>> make_value = lambda bin_: (bin_.mean, bin_.mean_error)

*get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate
of a graph point created from a histogram bin will be.
It can be "left" (default), "right" and "middle".

*field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
must be the same as the dimension of the result.
For a *make_value* above they would be
*("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

*scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
If it is ``True``, it uses the histogram scale.

*hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

Return the resulting graph.

def hist_to_graph(hist, make_value=None, get_coordinate="left",
                  field_names=("x", "y"), scale=None):
    """Convert a :class:`.histogram` to a :class:`.graph`.

    *make_value* is a function to set the value of a graph's point.
    By default it is bin content.
    *make_value* accepts a single value (bin content) without context.

    This option could be used to create graph's error bars.
    For example, to create a graph with errors
    from a histogram where bins contain
    a named tuple with fields *mean*, *mean_error* and a context
    one could use

    >>> make_value = lambda bin_: (bin_.mean, bin_.mean_error)

    *get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate
    of a graph point created from a histogram bin will be.
    It can be "left" (default), "right" and "middle".

    *field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
    must be the same as the dimension of the result.
    For a *make_value* above they would be
    *("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

    *scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
    If it is `True`, it uses the histogram scale.

    *hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
    or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

    Return the resulting graph.
    """
    if not hist:
        return []

    if not make_value:
        make_value = lambda bin_: bin_.bin

    if not field_names:
        field_names = ("x", "y")

    if not scale:
        scale = False

    if scale and not hasattr(hist, 'scale'):
        raise AttributeError("Histogram doesn't have a scale attribute")

    points = []

    for i, bin_ in enumerate(hist):
        x = get_coordinate == "left" and hist._index[i] or (get_coordinate == "right" and i + 1 or i)
        y = make_value(bin_)
        if isinstance(y, tuple) and len(y) != len(field_names):
            raise ValueError("make_value returned tuple with wrong number of fields")

        points.append(list(zip(field_names, y)))

    return points

    or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

    graph = Graph()
    if make_value is None:

    for bin_ in hist:

        graph.add(get_coordinate, x, y)

    from .. import graph

name: isoparse
docstring:
Parse an ISO-8601 datetime string into a :class:`datetime.datetime`.

An ISO-8601 datetime string consists of a date portion, followed
optionally by a time portion - the date and time portions are separated
by a single character separator, which is ``T`` in the official
standard. Incomplete date formats (such as ``YYYY-MM``) may *not* be
combined with a time portion.

Supported date formats are:

Common:

- ``YYYY``
- ``YYYY-MM`` or ``YYYYMM``
- ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or ``YYYYMMDD``

Uncommon:

- ``YYYY-Www`` or ``YYYYWww`` - ISO week (day defaults to 0)
- ``YYYY-Www-D`` or ``YYYYWwwD`` - ISO week and day

The ISO week and day numbering follows the same logic as
:func:`datetime.date.isocalendar`.

Supported time formats are:

- ``hh``
- ``hh:mm`` or ``hhmm``
- ``hh:mm:ss`` or ``hhmmss``
- ``hh:mm:ss.ssssss`` (Up to 6 sub-second digits)

Midnight is a special case for `hh`, as the standard supports both
00:00 and 24:00 as a representation. The decimal separator can be
either a dot or a comma.


.. caution::

    Support for fractional components other than seconds is part of the
    ISO-8601 standard, but is not currently implemented in this parser.

Supported time zone offset formats are:

- `Z` (UTC)
- `±HH:MM`
- `±HHMM`
- `±HH`

Offsets will be represented as :class:`dateutil.tz.tzoffset` objects,
with the exception of UTC, which will be represented as
:class:`dateutil.tz.tzutc`. Time zone offsets equivalent to UTC (such
as `+00:00`) will also be represented as :class:`dateutil.tz.tzutc`.

:param dt_str:
    A string or stream containing only an ISO-8601 datetime string

:return:
    Returns a :class:`datetime.datetime` representing the string.
    Unspecified components default to their lowest value.

.. warning::

    As of version 2.7.0, the strictness of the parser should not be
    considered a stable part of the contract. Any valid ISO-8601 string
    that parses correctly with the default settings will continue to
    parse correctly in future versions, but invalid strings that
    currently fail (e.g. ``2017-01-01T00:00+00:00:00``) are not
    guaranteed to continue failing in future versions if they encode
    a valid date.

def process_text_links(text):
    from lxml import etree
    from foiai.utils import get_attrib_value

    # Parse the HTML text with lxml
    tree = etree.HTML(text)
    links = tree.xpath('//a[contains(@href, "://")]')  # find all possible links

    # Iterate over each link and add the required attributes
    for link in links:
        href = link.get('href')
        rel = link.get('rel', 'noopener noreferrer')
        class_name = link.get('class')  # add a local class-based id

        # Add the new attributes to the link element
        link.set('aria-label', get_attrib_value(link, 'title') or get_attrib_value(link, 'alt'))
        link.set(' aria-expanded', 'false')
        link.set('aria-controls', class_name)  # link to a local button
        link.set('role', 'button')
        link.set('tabindex', '0')
        link.set('class', class_name)  # ensure it doesn't copy class from HTML

        # Wrap the original link text in a span and add a new button
        span = etree.Element('span')
        span.text = etree.CDATA(link.text)
        button = etree.Element('button')
        button.text = 'More >'
        button.set('class', class_name)
        button.set('data-foiai-link', href)
        button.set('aria-controls', class_name)  # link to the span containing the original text
        button.set('aria-expanded', 'false')
        button.set('aria-live', 'polite')
        button.set('aria-labelledby', class_name + '_label')
        button.set('tabindex', '0')
        span.append(button)
        link.clear()
        link.append(span)

    # Return the modified HTML text
    return etree.tostring(tree, encoding='unicode')

def retrieve_and_parse_diaspora_webfinger(handle):
    """
    Retrieve a and parse a remote Diaspora webfinger document.

    :arg handle: Remote handle to retrieve
    :returns: dict
    """
    url = f"https://www.diasporafoundation.org/api/oauth2/token?grant_type=password&client_id=diaspora&username={handle}&password=password"

    try:
        response = requests.post(url)
        response.raise_for_status()
        tokens = response.json()
        access_token = tokens['access_token']

        url = f"https://www.diasporafoundation.org/users/{handle}?access_token={access_token}&fields=bio,picture,profile"

        response = requests.get(url)
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = response.json()

        return data

    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"An error occurred while retrieving the Diaspora webfinger: {e}")
        return {}
